AI.motivation: The term "AI sycophancy" lacks a consistent definition and is applied to diverse behaviors (agreeing with false claims, excessive praise, withholding feedback), causing evaluation incomparability, non-transferable mitigations, and persistent sycophantic behaviors across systems.
AI.method: The authors reviewed 70 papers on AI sycophancy to develop a taxonomy with two axes: (1) whether sycophancy targets user beliefs/positions or personal traits/emotions, and (2) whether it manifests via explicit/direct language or implicit/subtle behaviors (framing, omission, tone). They also surveyed 106 experts to assess consensus on which behaviors qualify as sycophantic.
AI.result: Existing literature focuses on overt sycophancy toward users' beliefs; subtle and person-directed behaviors are understudied. 94.3% of 106 surveyed experts agree sycophancy is a significant problem, but they substantially disagree on which specific behaviors constitute sycophancy.
AI.conclusion: AI sycophancy is a broad family of behaviors with distinct measurement challenges, intervention requirements, and governance implications. The proposed taxonomy offers a shared vocabulary to systematically understand and address these varied behaviors.

title: TacO: Benchmarking Tactile Sensors for Object Manipulation
summary: Vision-based learning from demonstrations has achieved remarkable success in enabling robots to perform manipulation tasks and high-level semantic reasoning, yet it remains insufficient for complex, contact-rich manipulation. While there is broad agreement that tactile sensing improves manipulation, there is no empirical guidance on which tactile sensors are best suited for which manipulation tasks. In this paper, we provide a systematic, task-driven evaluation of tactile sensors for robot manipulation and propose a framework for selecting and evaluating sensors based on manipulation policy performance. Separate manipulation policies are trained for tactile sensors of four distinct modalities: visual, acoustic, magnetic, and resistive, across three tasks: pick-and-place with unknown mass, object reorientation, and plug insertion. For each task, an analysis of how sensor properties such as spatial resolution, shear sensing, and tactile representation, and the inherent material friction affect task performances is done. Rather than tactile sensing being universally beneficial in the same way, our results show that the usefulness of tactile information depends strongly on sensor modality, material properties, and the specific manipulation tasks. All of the tactile sensors, code, data, and hardware setup will be publicly available on the project website.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a systematic evaluation of four tactile sensor modalities (visual, acoustic, magnetic, resistive) across three manipulation tasks, finding that tactile sensing benefits vary significantly based on sensor modality, material properties, and task specifics.
AI.motivation: Vision-based learning from demonstrations is insufficient for complex, contact-rich manipulation. Despite consensus that tactile sensing improves manipulation, there is no empirical guidance on which tactile sensors are best suited for which tasks.
AI.method: Separate manipulation policies were trained for four tactile sensor modalities (visual, acoustic, magnetic, resistive) across three tasks: pick-and-place with unknown mass, object reorientation, and plug insertion. Analysis was performed on how sensor properties (spatial resolution, shear sensing, tactile representation, material friction) affect task performance.
AI.result: The usefulness of tactile information depends strongly on sensor modality, material properties, and the specific manipulation tasks, rather than tactile sensing being universally beneficial.
AI.conclusion: The paper proposes a framework for selecting and evaluating sensors based on manipulation policy performance, providing empirical guidance for sensor selection in contact-rich manipulation tasks.

title: Trace2Skill: Verifier-Guided Skill Evolution for Long-Context EDA Agents
summary: Complex Verilog Design Problems (CVDP) challenge hardware LLM agents because solving them requires localizing verifier-relevant RTL, testbenches, include paths, and build dependencies inside large repository snapshots, making precise edits, and recovering from sparse hidden-verifier failures. We present Trace2Skill, a test-time scaling framework that improves a hardware agent without RTL-specialized model fine-tuning. Rather than training a new model or only sampling more candidate solutions, Trace2Skill treats the agent's natural-language skill as an evolvable policy. It mines repeated rollout traces for success and failure modes, converts them into dense diagnostics and oracle lessons, and uses an oracle, mutator, and selector loop to produce task-specific skills that guide later search, editing, validation, and recovery. Because final pass/fail labels are often too coarse for hard failures, Trace2Skill also supports bounded runtime dense verifier feedback that returns sanitized functional observations while keeping hidden harnesses and reference solutions inaccessible to the agent. This feedback helps guide skill evolution and agent execution by connecting skill text, verifier evidence, and downstream behavior. Across hard CVDP tasks that defeat the seed CVDP agent, including tasks that also defeat frontier coding agents, Trace2Skill with dense verifier feedback substantially improves task pass rates and produces breakthrough passes on previously unsolved tasks, without requiring high-quality fine-tuning data, specialized RTL model training, or model weight updates. The same framework provides a general test-time scaling strategy that can extend beyond digital design to other verifiable EDA tasks.

AI.tldr: Trace2Skill is a test-time scaling framework that improves hardware LLM agents on complex Verilog design tasks by mining rollout traces, converting them into task-specific skills via oracle-mutator-selector loop, and using dense verifier feedback—achieving breakthrough results without model fine-tuning or RTL-specialized training.
AI.motivation: Complex Verilog Design Problems (CVDP) are difficult for hardware LLM agents due to the need to localize verifier-relevant RTL, testbenches, include paths, and build dependencies in large repos, make precise edits, and recover from sparse hidden-verifier failures. Existing approaches (training new models or sampling more solutions) are insufficient.
AI.method: Trace2Skill treats the agent's natural-language skill as an evolvable policy. It mines repeated rollout traces for success/failure modes, converts them into dense diagnostics and oracle lessons, and uses an oracle, mutator, and selector loop to produce task-specific skills. It also supports bounded runtime dense verifier feedback that returns sanitized functional observations while keeping hidden harnesses and reference solutions inaccessible.
AI.result: Across hard CVDP tasks that defeat the seed agent (including tasks that defeat frontier coding agents), Trace2Skill with dense verifier feedback substantially improves task pass rates and produces breakthrough passes on previously unsolved tasks.
AI.conclusion: Trace2Skill provides a general test-time scaling strategy that can extend beyond digital design to other verifiable EDA tasks, without requiring high-quality fine-tuning data, specialized RTL model training, or model weight updates.

title: Industrial Dual-Arm Box Handling via Online Inertial Estimation and Convex Wrench Optimization
comment: 14 pages, submitted to Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing (RCIM) Journal
summary: Industrial robotic object handling often involves boxes and packages whose mass and center of mass are not known in advance. These uncertainties affect the force--moment balance required for stable lifting, and improper regulation of contact wrenches can lead to slip, object drop, orientation deviation, or excessive squeezing. This paper presents a friction-aware dual-arm box-handling framework for objects with unknown inertial properties. The proposed approach estimates the object mass and center of mass online from measured contact wrenches, and computes friction-feasible contact forces and torsional moments through a second-order cone program (SOCP) under ellipsoidal friction-limit-surface constraints. An offline trajectory refinement stage is also included to reduce undesired object--environment contact when geometric constraints are present. By enforcing friction feasibility as a hard constraint and minimizing contact effort within the feasible region, the framework achieves stable lifting without treating slip avoidance and excessive squeezing as separately tuned objectives. Experiments on a real dual-arm robotic system under different center-of-mass configurations demonstrate that the method lifts objects with unknown inertial properties while maintaining stable frictional contact.

AI.tldr: A friction-aware dual-arm box-handling framework that estimates unknown mass and center of mass online, computes friction-feasible contact forces via SOCP under ellipsoidal friction-limit-surface constraints, and achieves stable lifting without separately tuning slip and squeeze objectives.
AI.motivation: Industrial robotic object handling involves boxes/packages with unknown mass and center of mass, which cause uncertainties in force-moment balance for stable lifting and can lead to slip, dropping, orientation deviation, or excessive squeezing.
AI.method: Online estimation of object mass and center of mass from measured contact wrenches; friction-feasible contact forces and torsional moments computed via a second-order cone program (SOCP) under ellipsoidal friction-limit-surface constraints; offline trajectory refinement to reduce undesired object-environment contact.
AI.result: Experiments on a real dual-arm robotic system under different center-of-mass configurations demonstrate that the method lifts objects with unknown inertial properties while maintaining stable frictional contact.
AI.conclusion: Enforcing friction feasibility as a hard constraint and minimizing contact effort within the feasible region achieves stable lifting without treating slip avoidance and excessive squeezing as separately tuned objectives.

title: Implicit Safety Alignment from Crowd Preferences
comment: Accepted to ICML 2026. Conference paper
summary: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) can reveal implicit objectives such as safety considerations that go beyond task completion. In this work, we focus on the common safety criteria embedded in crowd preference datasets, where different users may express distinct preferences or objectives, yet follow similar safety principles. Our aim is to discover shared safety criteria from crowd preferences and then transfer them to downstream RL tasks to regularize agent behavior and enforce safety. We first show that direct reward combination-optimizing a preference-learned reward model together with downstream task rewards-has inherent limitations. Motivated by this, we propose Safe Crowd Preference-based RL, a hierarchical framework that extracts safety-aligned skills from crowd preferences and composes them via a high-level policy to safely solve downstream tasks. Experiments across safe RL environments and a preliminary LLM-style task with diverse user goals and shared safety constraints demonstrate that our approach substantially lowers safety costs without access to explicit safety rewards, while achieving task performance comparable to oracle methods trained with ground-truth safety signals.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical framework that extracts safety-aligned skills from crowd preferences and composes them via a high-level policy to safely solve downstream RL tasks, outperforming direct reward combination approaches and reducing safety costs without explicit safety rewards.
AI.motivation: To discover shared safety criteria embedded in crowd preference datasets and transfer them to downstream RL tasks to regularize agent behavior and enforce safety, addressing the limitations of direct reward combination approaches.
AI.method: Safe Crowd Preference-based RL (SCP-RL), a hierarchical framework that extracts safety-aligned skills from crowd preferences and composes them via a high-level policy for safe downstream task solving.
AI.result: Substantially lowers safety costs without access to explicit safety rewards, while achieving task performance comparable to oracle methods trained with ground-truth safety signals across safe RL environments and a preliminary LLM-style task.
AI.conclusion: Direct reward combination has inherent limitations, and the proposed hierarchical framework effectively transfers shared safety criteria from crowd preferences to downstream tasks, enabling safe RL without explicit safety reward signals.

title: CoRMA: Contrastive RMA for Contact-Rich Meta-Adaptation
summary: We present CoRMA(Contrastive Robotic Motor Adaptation), a context-based meta-adaptation framework that modifies RMA for force-dominant assembly. CoRMA replaces raw simulator-parameter adaptation with a compact 6D simulator-only semantic contact context describing contact onset, lateral engagement, guided transition, contact direction, and jamming. A deployable causal Transformer adapter infers this context online from force, proprioceptive, and action histories using semantic regression and a force-regime contrastive objective. At deployment, oracle context is removed and replaced by the inferred context, enabling within-episode adaptation without demonstrations, privileged inputs, or gradient updates. We evaluate CoRMA on PegInsert, GearMesh, and NutThread in Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim~5.0 and on a real Marvin arm. Compared with FORGE baselines that achieve high simulation success but degrade substantially on hardware, CoRMA retains higher verified real success under controlled target-pose noise. These results support semantic contact inference as a reusable adaptation interface within a related assembly task family, while broader unseen-task generalization and Real2Sim calibration remain future work.

AI.tldr: CoRMA is a contrastive meta-adaptation framework that replaces raw simulator parameters with a 6D semantic contact context, using a causal Transformer to infer this context online for force-dominant robotic assembly tasks, achieving better real-world success than FORGE baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing RMA-based methods and FORGE baselines suffer from simulation-to-reality transfer degradation in force-dominant assembly tasks. The paper aims to replace brittle raw simulator parameter adaptation with a reusable, semantic contact inference interface that generalizes within a task family without demonstrations or privileged inputs.
AI.method: CoRMA proposes a context-based meta-adaptation framework: (1) a compact 6D simulator-only semantic contact context (contact onset, lateral engagement, guided transition, contact direction, jamming); (2) a deployable causal Transformer adapter that infers this context online from force, proprioceptive, and action histories via semantic regression and a force-regime contrastive objective; (3) at deployment, oracle context is removed and replaced by inferred context, enabling within-episode adaptation without demonstrations, privileged inputs, or gradient updates.
AI.result: Evaluated on PegInsert, GearMesh, and NutThread in Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim 5.0 and on a real Marvin arm. CoRMA retains higher verified real success under controlled target-pose noise compared to FORGE baselines, which achieve high simulation success but degrade substantially on hardware.
AI.conclusion: Semantic contact inference serves as a reusable adaptation interface within a related assembly task family. Broader unseen-task generalization and Real2Sim calibration remain future work.

title: Toward AI VIS Co-Scientists: A General and End-to-End Agent Harness for Solving Complex Data Visualization Tasks
summary: The ability to inspect, interpret, and communicate complex data is crucial for virtually any scientific endeavor, but often requires significant expertise outside the core domain ranging from data management and analysis to visualization design and implementation. We present an end-to-end agentic harness that, based on only the data and a high level description of the tasks, independently designs custom visual analysis applications (VIS apps). This represents an important step towards a general AI co-scientist envisioned by many as an autonomous system that can autonomously execute long horizon tasks based on high-level directions. Our proposed VIS co-scientist is an essential component of this broader AI co-scientist vision: a harness that can autonomously analyze data and design visualization solutions using a collection of agents and specialized skills that coordinate exploratory analysis, plan, configure the environment, implement, validate the interface, and most importantly evaluate the overall task completion. Each stage produces document and instruction artifacts that guide downstream work and enable iterative refinement. We validate this approach on IEEE SciVis Contests spanning multiple science and engineering fields. These contests serve as ideal proving grounds because they encode real-world complexity: ambiguous requirements, diverse data modalities, design trade-offs, and task-driven validation. Given only the data and target tasks, our system autonomously produces functional single-page VIS Apps with verified linked-view behavior, highly customized to domain experts' specified tasks and needs.

AI.tldr: Presents an end-to-end agentic system that autonomously designs custom visual analysis applications from just data and high-level task descriptions, validated on IEEE SciVis Contests.
AI.motivation: Inspecting, interpreting, and communicating complex data requires expertise beyond core domain knowledge (data management, analysis, visualization design). The goal is to create an autonomous AI co-scientist that can execute long-horizon tasks from high-level directions.
AI.method: An end-to-end agentic harness (VIS co-scientist) using a collection of agents and specialized skills that coordinate: exploratory analysis, planning, environment configuration, implementation, interface validation, and overall task completion evaluation. Each stage produces documents/instructions for downstream work and iterative refinement.
AI.result: Validated on IEEE SciVis Contests: the system autonomously produces functional single-page VIS Apps with verified linked-view behavior, highly customized to domain experts' specified tasks and needs, given only data and target tasks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VIS co-scientist represents an important step toward a general AI co-scientist—an autonomous system that can analyze data and design visualization solutions from high-level directions, successfully handling real-world complexity including ambiguous requirements, diverse data modalities, design trade-offs, and task-driven validation.

title: Beyond Pixels: Learning Invariant Rewards for Real-World Robotics From a Few Demonstrations
summary: Designing reward functions that generalize beyond controlled laboratory settings remains a fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning for robotics. In open-world manipulation problems, a single task can appear in numerous variants through different object instances, positions, and camera viewpoints. Recent vision-based reward models tend to memorize specific pixel distributions and fail to generalize beyond their training conditions. To address this, we propose a framework that learns invariant symbolic reward functions from as few as five demonstrations. The insight is to shift from visual feature-fitting to the discovery of behavioral invariants: task-level properties that remain constant across diverse visual instantiations. The framework has two coupled components: a structural reward formulation that encodes task-level strategies and physical constraints while preserving optimal policy invariance, and a hybrid symbolic-numerical procedure that distills these invariants from demonstrations without online interaction. Experiments on eight Meta-World tasks and three Franka manipulation tasks demonstrate that our method achieves stronger process alignment and policy rollout ranking abilities compared to baselines, accelerating downstream policy learning. Three real-world out-of-distribution experiments further show that the same learned reward generalizes zero-shot to position, viewpoint, and object variations, enabling a single reward representation to be reused across diverse task variants in practice.

AI.tldr: A framework that learns invariant symbolic reward functions from as few as five demonstrations by discovering behavioral invariants (task-level properties constant across visual variations), using a structural reward formulation and hybrid symbolic-numerical distillation, achieving zero-shot generalization to out-of-distribution variations in real-world manipulation tasks.
AI.motivation: Designing reward functions that generalize beyond controlled lab settings remains a fundamental challenge in robotics RL; vision-based reward models tend to memorize specific pixel distributions and fail to generalize across different object instances, positions, and camera viewpoints in open-world manipulation problems.
AI.method: A framework with two coupled components: (1) a structural reward formulation that encodes task-level strategies and physical constraints while preserving optimal policy invariance, and (2) a hybrid symbolic-numerical procedure that distills behavioral invariants from as few as five demonstrations without online interaction.
AI.result: Outperforms baselines in process alignment and policy rollout ranking on eight Meta-World and three Franka manipulation tasks, accelerating downstream policy learning. Zero-shot generalization to position, viewpoint, and object variations in three real-world out-of-distribution experiments.
AI.conclusion: The method shifts from visual feature-fitting to discovering behavioral invariants, enabling a single learned reward representation to be reused across diverse task variants in practice, demonstrating strong generalization without requiring additional data or fine-tuning.

title: FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation
summary: Modern recommender systems rely heavily on ID-based collaborative filtering: each item is represented by a unique ID embedding that accumulates collaborative signals from user interactions. Livestreaming recommendation, however, faces a unique challenge in this paradigm: a live room typically broadcasts for only tens of minutes, so its item ID remains poorly learned in a persistent cold-start state and ID-centric ranking models fail to generalize. We present FLUID, the first framework to fully retire the candidate-side item ID from a production-scale livestreaming ranker. FLUID couples a cross-domain multimodal encoder, jointly trained on short videos and livestreams to produce discrete hierarchical codes (LUCID), with a late-fusion, ID-free design that injects slice-level and room-level LUCID as independent tokens, stabilized by a staged warmup under online incremental training. Deployed on our industrial livestreaming recommenders with a cross-platform combined user base of over one billion globally, FLUID delivers significant online gains of +0.55% Quality Watch Duration, +2.05% Cold-Start Room Views, and +0.05% Active Hours.

AI.tldr: FLUID is the first framework to fully remove item IDs from a production-scale livestreaming ranker, using a cross-domain multimodal encoder with discrete hierarchical codes (LUCID) and a late-fusion, ID-free design, achieving significant gains in cold-start recommendation quality for over one billion global users.
AI.motivation: Livestreaming recommendation suffers from persistent cold-start problems because live rooms last only tens of minutes, making traditional ID-based collaborative filtering embeddings poorly learned and unable to generalize.
AI.method: FLUID eliminates candidate-side item IDs entirely. It couples a cross-domain multimodal encoder (jointly trained on short videos and livestreams) that produces discrete hierarchical codes (LUCID), with a late-fusion, ID-free design that injects slice-level and room-level LUCID as independent tokens, stabilized by staged warmup under online incremental training.
AI.result: Deployed on industrial livestreaming recommenders with a cross-platform user base of over one billion globally, achieving +0.55% Quality Watch Duration, +2.05% Cold-Start Room Views, and +0.05% Active Hours.
AI.conclusion: Fully retiring item IDs in favor of multimodal discrete codes effectively solves the persistent cold-start problem in livestreaming recommendation at production scale.

title: Action with Visual Primitives
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Project page: https://kingdroper.github.io/AVP/
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for generalist robotic manipulation. A common design in current architectures maps language instructions and visual observations to actions in a single forward pass. While conceptually simple, this formulation entangles instruction comprehension, spatial scene understanding, and motor control within a single learning objective. As a result, the action expert must implicitly relearn cognitive and perceptual capabilities already present in the pretrained VLM, which can limit both learning efficiency and generalization. We introduce AVP (Action with Visual Primitives), an end-to-end architecture that implements this visual-primitive-centric interface: the VLM infers the next-stage target and emits visual-primitive tokens that condition a flow-matching action expert, with supervision derived from end-effector kinematics. Real-robot experiments on general pick-and-place tasks show that AVP improves the success rate by 27.61% over pi_0.5 and outperforms other recent methods, with consistent gains in data efficiency, spatial-compositional generalization, and object-level transfer.

AI.tldr: AVP introduces a visual-primitive-centric interface where a VLM emits visual tokens to condition a flow-matching action expert, decoupling cognitive/perceptual reasoning from motor control, improving success rate by 27.61% over pi_0.5 in pick-and-place tasks.
AI.motivation: Current VLA models entangle instruction comprehension, spatial understanding, and motor control in a single learning objective, forcing the action expert to implicitly relearn cognitive and perceptual capabilities already present in the pretrained VLM, limiting learning efficiency and generalization.
AI.method: AVP architecture: the VLM infers the next-stage target and emits visual-primitive tokens that condition a flow-matching action expert, with supervision derived from end-effector kinematics. This implements a visual-primitive-centric interface that decouples high-level reasoning from low-level control.
AI.result: Real-robot pick-and-place experiments show AVP improves success rate by 27.61% over pi_0.5, with consistent gains in data efficiency, spatial-compositional generalization, and object-level transfer.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling cognitive/perceptual reasoning from motor control via visual-primitive tokens is an effective design paradigm for generalist robotic manipulation, achieving superior performance and generalization.

title: Planning in the LLM Era: Building for Reliability and Efficiency
comment: Published at ICAPS 2026
summary: Growing attention to intelligent agents has put a spotlight on one of their central capabilities: planning. Early attempts to leverage large language models (LLMs) for planning relied on single-shot plan generation, followed by hybrid approaches that coupled LLMs with limited external search. These methods, unsound and incomplete by their very nature, often require substantial resources without yielding better solutions on unseen problems. As the limitations of LLMs become clearer, recent work has shifted toward using them at solution construction time -- generating symbolic solvers for a family of problems that can be verified and then used efficiently at inference time. This trend reflects the growing need for agents that are both reliable and resource-efficient. It also offers a path towards generating maintainable planners with minimal dependence on language models at inference time. In this paper, we argue that this shift reflects a broader realignment of the planning field in the LLM era. We examine three major categories of planner-generation methods, discuss their current limitations, and outline research steps towards a more reliable and efficient LLM-based generation of planners.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that LLM-based planning is shifting from using LLMs directly for plan generation to using them for generating symbolic planners that are verified and efficient at inference time, reflecting a broader realignment toward reliability and resource efficiency.
AI.motivation: Growing interest in intelligent agents has highlighted planning as a core capability, but early LLM-based planning approaches (single-shot generation, hybrid search) are unsound, incomplete, and resource-intensive, motivating the need for more reliable and efficient methods.
AI.method: The paper categorizes planner-generation methods into three major categories, analyzes their limitations, and outlines research directions for more reliable and efficient LLM-based generation of planners.
AI.result: Identifies a trend shift toward using LLMs at solution construction time to generate symbolic solvers that can be verified and used efficiently at inference, minimizing reliance on LLMs during inference.
AI.conclusion: The field is realigning toward generating maintainable, verifiable planners with minimal inference-time dependence on LLMs, offering a path toward more reliable and resource-efficient agents.

title: Learning A Unified Risk Map for Autonomous Driving in Partially Observable Environments
comment: Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
summary: Occlusion-aware prediction remains a critical challenge in autonomous driving due to the inherent uncertainty of unobserved regions. Existing approaches either overestimate risk based on reachable states or struggle to predict accurate trajectories under high occlusion uncertainty. To address these limitations, we propose a unified risk map modeling and learning framework for partially observable environments. Our method integrates traffic flow risk and collision risk through spatiotemporal modeling, enabling fine-grained assessment of occlusion-induced hazards. To address the scarcity of scenarios involving occluded interactions, we introduce a diffusion-based scenario generation framework that produces realistic yet adversarial scenarios. We integrate the modeling and learning of a unified risk map into a framework that supports risk-aware planning under partial observability. Experiments on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset show that our method significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art occlusion-aware baseline, improving minimum time-to-collision by 0.78 times and average time-to-collision by 1.67 times. The proposed framework offers a comprehensive and practical solution for risk-aware planning in partially observable environments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a unified risk map framework for occlusion-aware prediction in autonomous driving, integrating traffic flow and collision risks via spatiotemporal modeling, using a diffusion-based scenario generator for adversarial occluded interactions, and significantly outperforming baselines on Waymo Open Motion Dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing occlusion-aware prediction methods either overestimate risk based on reachable states or fail to predict accurate trajectories under high occlusion uncertainty, lacking a unified risk assessment framework for partially observable environments.
AI.method: The method integrates traffic flow risk and collision risk through spatiotemporal modeling into a unified risk map, employs a diffusion-based scenario generation framework to produce realistic yet adversarial occluded interaction scenarios, and supports risk-aware planning under partial observability.
AI.result: On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, the method improves minimum time-to-collision by 0.78 times and average time-to-collision by 1.67 times over state-of-the-art occlusion-aware baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers a comprehensive and practical solution for risk-aware planning in partially observable environments, effectively addressing occlusion-induced hazards.

title: AI-Enabled Serious Games: Integrating Intelligence and Adaptivity in Training Systems
comment: Book chapter, 1 figure. To appear in "Advances in Global Applied Artificial Intelligence," G. A. Tsihrintzis, M. Virvou, N. G. Bourbakis, and L. C. Jain (Eds.), Springer, Learning and Analytics in Intelligent Systems book series, 2026
summary: Serious games are widely used for learning and training across domains such as healthcare, defense, and education. Persistent challenges remain, however, including static scenario design, authoring bottlenecks, limited learner modeling, and difficulty implementing meaningful real-time instructional adaptation. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) introduce novel capabilities such as dynamic scenario variation, contextual feedback, adaptive pacing, and learner-state modeling that may help address some of these limitations. At the same time, integrating AI into serious games raises important questions related to validity, transparency, system control, and learner trust. This chapter examines how contemporary AI approaches may support real-time instructional adaptation in serious games. It distinguishes between instructional intelligence, defined as a system's capacity to infer learner knowledge and reason about pedagogically appropriate responses, and adaptivity, defined as the ability to modify instructional actions during interaction. A historical synthesis of adaptive learning systems is presented, tracing developments from early computer-assisted instruction through intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), dynamic difficulty adjustment (DDA), authoring platforms, learning analytics, and recent AI-enabled architectures. Building on this perspective, the chapter discusses how large language models (LLMs), reinforcement learning (RL), and agent-based architectures may contribute to more integrated forms of intelligence and adaptivity in serious games. It also highlights practical and research challenges associated with AI-enabled systems, including explainability, validation, computational cost, and the limited empirical evidence regarding long-term learning outcomes in AI-enabled serious games.

AI.tldr: This chapter examines how AI approaches (LLMs, RL, agent-based architectures) can enable real-time instructional adaptation in serious games, distinguishing between instructional intelligence (inferring learner knowledge and reasoning about pedagogical responses) and adaptivity (modifying actions during interaction). It provides a historical synthesis from early CAI to modern AI-enabled systems, and discusses challenges including explainability, validation, computational cost, and limited evidence on long-term learning outcomes.
AI.motivation: Serious games face persistent challenges including static scenario design, authoring bottlenecks, limited learner modeling, and difficulty implementing meaningful real-time instructional adaptation. AI advances may help address these limitations.
AI.method: Historical synthesis tracing developments from computer-assisted instruction through intelligent tutoring systems, dynamic difficulty adjustment, authoring platforms, learning analytics, and recent AI-enabled architectures. Discussion of specific AI approaches: LLMs, reinforcement learning, and agent-based architectures.
AI.result: Identifies that AI approaches (LLMs, RL, agent-based architectures) may contribute to more integrated forms of intelligence and adaptivity in serious games, but significant challenges remain including explainability, validation, computational cost, and lack of empirical evidence on long-term learning outcomes.
AI.conclusion: AI offers potential for real-time instructional adaptation in serious games, but practical and research challenges around validity, transparency, system control, learner trust, and empirical validation of long-term effectiveness must be addressed.

title: Imagine2Real: Towards Zero-shot Humanoid-Object Interaction via Video Generative Priors
summary: Whole-body Humanoid-Object Interaction (HOI) is bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-fidelity 3D data. While video generative priors offer a promising alternative, existing methods suffer from \textit{Representation Misalignment} due to their reliance on geometric priors (e.g., explicit CAD models), and \textit{Retargeting Complexity} arising from intensive morphing and morphological mismatch. We propose Imagine2Real, a zero-shot HOI framework for flexible, geometry-free interaction. To resolve misalignment, we formulate robot and object motions as unified 4D point trajectories. To overcome retargeting complexity, our Keypoints Tracker tracks only sparse critical points (base, hands, and object), entirely bypassing the error-amplifying retargeting process. To maintain natural gaits despite these sparse signals, we utilize the latent space of a Behavior Foundation Model (BFM) as the tracker's search domain. Using a progressive training strategy, Imagine2Real learns robust behaviors with simple tracking rewards, enabling zero-shot physical deployment within a motion capture(mocap) system.

AI.tldr: Imagine2Real is a zero-shot HOI framework that uses unified 4D point trajectories and a Keypoints Tracker with Behavior Foundation Model latent space to enable geometry-free, retargeting-free humanoid-object interaction from video priors.
AI.motivation: Video generative priors offer a promising alternative for HOI data, but existing methods face Representation Misalignment (reliance on geometric priors like CAD models) and Retargeting Complexity (intensive morphing and morphological mismatch).
AI.method: Formulates robot and object motions as unified 4D point trajectories; uses Keypoints Tracker tracking only sparse critical points (base, hands, object) to bypass retargeting; leverages Behavior Foundation Model (BFM) latent space as search domain; employs progressive training strategy with simple tracking rewards.
AI.result: Enables zero-shot physical deployment within a motion capture system, learning robust behaviors from sparse signals.
AI.conclusion: Imagine2Real achieves flexible, geometry-free HOI by eliminating retargeting complexity and representation alignment issues through sparse keypoint tracking in BFM latent space.

title: Format-Constraint Coupling in Knowledge Graph Construction from Statistical Tables
comment: 8 pages main body, 18 pages appendices. Submitted to EMNLP 2026 via ACL Rolling Review (ARR). Corresponding author: Yuxiang Feng (yxfeng@scut.edu.cn). Code and data available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/sge_lightrag-BE19
summary: An extraction schema should not reduce knowledge graph fidelity. On statistical CSV, however, it can. We study country-by-year time-series matrices, a common layout on open-data portals. In this setting, serialization format and schema constraints interact super-additively. Their joint effect exceeds the sum of independent effects by up to +1.180 (2x2 factorial, 6 datasets). Bootstrap 95% CIs are strictly positive on 4/6 datasets, with strongest evidence on wide Type-II matrices. More critically, a schema applied to a mismatched format can trigger catastrophic mismatch. Fact coverage falls below the unconstrained baseline on 4/6 datasets through entity inflation or extraction refusal. We call this observed pattern format-constraint coupling. Probing and token ablation support a surface-form anchoring explanation centred on column-name references. Controlled variants across format-schema pairings, GraphRAG hosts, and LLM families show the same direction within the measured scope; one LLM family shows only partial activation. The observation also has a diagnostic consequence. Three standard retrieval modes largely mask construction quality (delta <= 1pp), whereas direct graph access exposes gaps up to +47.6pp (p < 0.0001). To support fidelity-aware evaluation, we release CSVFidelity-Bench. It contains 15 datasets, 11 Type-II matrices, 4 Type-III tables, and 1,892 Gold Standard facts across 6 domains.

AI.tldr: Schema constraints applied to CSV time-series matrices can reduce knowledge graph fidelity through format-constraint coupling, where mismatched format-schema pairings cause catastrophic coverage drops. Direct graph access reveals construction quality gaps up to +47.6pp that retrieval modes mask. CSVFidelity-Bench is released for fidelity-aware evaluation.
AI.motivation: Schema constraints should not reduce knowledge graph fidelity, but on statistical CSV (country-by-year time-series matrices) they can. The paper investigates how serialization format and schema constraints interact super-additively, potentially causing catastrophic mismatch.
AI.method: 2x2 factorial experiment across 6 datasets; bootstrap CIs; probing and token ablation for surface-form anchoring explanation; controlled variants across format-schema pairings, GraphRAG hosts, and LLM families; comparison of three retrieval modes vs. direct graph access.
AI.result: Joint effect of format and schema exceeds sum of independent effects by up to +1.180. Schema on mismatched format reduces fact coverage on 4/6 datasets via entity inflation or extraction refusal. Retrieval modes mask construction quality (delta <= 1pp), while direct graph access exposes gaps up to +47.6pp (p < 0.0001).
AI.conclusion: The paper identifies format-constraint coupling as a phenomenon degrading KG fidelity, explains it via surface-form anchoring (column-name references), and contributes CSVFidelity-Bench (15 datasets, 1,892 Gold Standard facts) for fidelity-aware evaluation.

title: Spatial Memory for Out-of-Vision Manipulation in Vision-Language-Action
comment: Accepted by ICML 2026
summary: We introduce SOMA, the Spatial Memory framework for Out-of-Vision Manipulation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. Most existing VLAs implicitly assume that task-relevant objects are always visible, leading to brittle and reactive behaviors when targets fall outside the camera's field of view. SOMA addresses this limitation by equipping VLAs with a persistent spatial memory constructed from multi-view observations acquired via a movable head camera, enabling reasoning beyond the current visual frustum. The framework consists of three components: Spatial Memory Construction, which aggregates angular-wise observations into a unified spatial-semantic representation through scanning; Dynamic Memory Refinement, which maintains global consistency over time; and Contextual Memory Retrieval, which activates instruction-relevant spatial cues during manipulation. We evaluate SOMA on five challenging real-world out-of-vision manipulation tasks, including multi-step and dual-arm scenarios where target objects are initially invisible. Experimental results show that SOMA not only improves task success rates, but also induces qualitatively different manipulation behaviors, with faster target localization, reduced viewpoint search, and near one-shot grasping under partial observability. Additional experiments on RoboCasa GR1 and SimplerEnv further validate the effectiveness of SOMA's memory design under conventional fully observable settings. Code will be released soon.

AI.tldr: SOMA is a spatial memory framework that enables Vision-Language-Action models to reason about objects outside the camera's field of view by constructing, refining, and retrieving persistent spatial-semantic representations from multi-view observations, improving manipulation success rates and enabling one-shot grasping under partial observability.
AI.motivation: Existing VLA models implicitly assume task-relevant objects are always visible, leading to brittle and reactive behaviors when targets fall outside the camera's field of view. SOMA addresses this limitation by equipping VLAs with persistent spatial memory for reasoning beyond the current visual frustum.
AI.method: SOMA consists of three components: (1) Spatial Memory Construction — aggregates angular-wise observations into a unified spatial-semantic representation via scanning with a movable head camera; (2) Dynamic Memory Refinement — maintains global consistency over time; (3) Contextual Memory Retrieval — activates instruction-relevant spatial cues during manipulation.
AI.result: SOMA improves task success rates on five challenging real-world out-of-vision manipulation tasks (multi-step and dual-arm scenarios). It induces qualitatively different behaviors: faster target localization, reduced viewpoint search, and near one-shot grasping under partial observability. Additional experiments on RoboCasa GR1 and SimplerEnv confirm effectiveness in fully observable settings.
AI.conclusion: SOMA effectively bridges the gap between reactive and memory-driven manipulation in VLAs, enabling robust performance even when target objects are initially invisible, while also benefiting conventional fully observable settings.

title: Echo: Learning from Experience Data via User-Driven Refinement
summary:
Static "human data" faces inherent limitations: it is expensive to scale and bounded by the knowledge of its creators. Continuous learning from "experience data" - interactions between agents and their environments - promises to transcend these barriers. Today, the widespread deployment of AI agents grants us low-cost access to massive streams of such real-world experience. However, raw interaction logs are inherently noisy, filled with trial-and-error and low information density, rendering them inefficient for direct model training.
  We introduce Echo, a generalized framework designed to operationalize the transition from raw experience to learnable knowledge, effectively "echoing" environmental feedback back into the training loop for model optimization. In today's agent ecosystem, user refinement serves as a primary source of such feedback: driven by responsibility for the outcome, users rigorously transform flawed agent proposals into verified solutions. These user-driven refinement sequences inherently distill agents' crude attempts into high-quality training signals. Echo systematically harvests these signals to continuously align the agent with real-world needs. Large-scale validation in a production code completion environment confirms that Echo effectively harnesses this pipeline, breaking the static performance ceiling by increasing the acceptance rate from 25.7% to 35.7%.

AI.tldr: Echo is a generalized framework that transforms noisy real-world agent interaction logs into learnable training signals by harvesting user refinement sequences, enabling continuous model alignment and breaking static performance ceilings (25.7% → 35.7% acceptance rate in code completion).
AI.motivation: Static human data is expensive to scale and bounded by creator knowledge. While massive streams of real-world agent experience data are now available, raw interaction logs are inherently noisy, filled with trial-and-error and low information density, making them inefficient for direct model training.
AI.method: Echo operationalizes the transition from raw experience to learnable knowledge by systematically harvesting user-driven refinement sequences. User refinement serves as a primary feedback source—users transform flawed agent proposals into verified solutions, and these sequences distill agents' crude attempts into high-quality training signals for continuous alignment.
AI.result: Large-scale validation in a production code completion environment shows Echo increases acceptance rate from 25.7% to 35.7%, breaking the static performance ceiling.
AI.conclusion: Echo effectively harnesses user refinement as a feedback pipeline to continuously align agents with real-world needs, overcoming the limitations of static human data.

title: How can reasoning capability empower the AI copilot robot in endoscopic surgery
comment: Accepted by npj digital medicine
summary: Reasoning capability has significantly advanced complex logical inference and robotic decision-making in general domains. However, its potential in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) copilot robot-particularly implemented based on the Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model-remains unexplored in endoscopic surgery. Effective reasoning should enable AI copilot robots to integrate multimodal cues, interpret surgical intent, and infer hidden tissue dynamics, thereby alleviating intraoperative uncertainty and cognitive burden on surgeons. Properly implemented, reasoning-driven autonomy can transform AI copilot robots from reactive executors into cognitive collaborators, enhancing precision, safety, and sustainability in clinical practice.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the potential of reasoning capability (specifically in VLA-based AI copilot robots) to enhance endoscopic surgery by integrating multimodal cues, interpreting surgical intent, and inferring hidden tissue dynamics, thereby transforming AI from reactive executors into cognitive collaborators for improved precision and safety.
AI.motivation: To address the unexplored potential of reasoning in VLA-based AI copilot robots for endoscopic surgery, aiming to alleviate intraoperative uncertainty and cognitive burden on surgeons.
AI.method: Leveraging reasoning capability within a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model framework to integrate multimodal cues, interpret surgical intent, and infer hidden tissue dynamics.
AI.result: Not explicitly reported in the abstract; the paper appears to be a position/vision paper proposing the concept rather than presenting empirical results.
AI.conclusion: Reasoning-driven autonomy can transform AI copilot robots from reactive executors into cognitive collaborators, enhancing precision, safety, and sustainability in clinical endoscopic surgery.

title: Real-Time Auto-Optimization in Unknown Environments via Structure-Exploiting Dual Control for Exploration and Exploitation
summary: This paper develops a fast numerical dual control for exploration and exploitation (DCEE) method to address auto-optimization problems in unknown environments. In auto-optimization problems, the optimal operating condition is unknown a priori and may vary with the environment. As in classical dual control techniques, computational burden remains a major concern in DCEE for active learning. Existing DCEE methods provide a principled exploration-exploitation objective, but mainly realized through standard optimization packages or explicit gradient-type update laws, where the numerical structure of the DCEE has not been fully exploited. This paper shows that the reward function in DCEE has an inherent convex-over-nonlinear structure, where the exploitation and exploration terms form a unified nonlinear residual map equipped with a convex outer loss. Benefiting from this structure, a structure-exploiting numerical method is developed by linearizing only the nonlinear residual map while preserving the convex outer loss. Thus, each subproblem is transformed into a structured convex form that can be solved reliably. The resulting generalized Gauss-Newton Hessian approximation is positive semidefinite and depends only on first-order derivatives, thereby supporting fast online computation. The proposed method is evaluated on a vehicle cruising auto-optimization problem and compared with existing methods. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experimental results show that the proposed method improves control performance and achieves a speedup of approximately one order of magnitude, with a microsecond-level maximum computation time of only 83 μs on a typical vehicle embedded CPU.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a fast numerical DCEE method for auto-optimization in unknown environments, exploiting a convex-over-nonlinear structure in the reward function to achieve a generalized Gauss-Newton solver. The method achieves microsecond-level computation (83 μs max) and ~10x speedup over existing methods, validated on vehicle cruising problems via simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiments.
AI.motivation: Computational burden limits the practical deployment of dual control for exploration and exploitation (DCEE) methods in real-time auto-optimization problems, as existing approaches rely on standard optimization packages or explicit gradient updates without exploiting the underlying numerical structure.
AI.method: The paper identifies an inherent convex-over-nonlinear structure in the DCEE reward function, where exploitation and exploration form a unified nonlinear residual map with a convex outer loss. A structure-exploiting numerical method is developed by linearizing only the nonlinear residual map while preserving the convex outer loss, converting each subproblem into a structured convex form solvable via a generalized Gauss-Newton method with a positive semidefinite Hessian approximation dependent only on first-order derivatives.
AI.result: On a vehicle cruising auto-optimization problem, the proposed method achieves approximately one order of magnitude speedup over existing methods, with a maximum computation time of only 83 μs on a typical vehicle embedded CPU, as demonstrated in both simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed structure-exploiting numerical DCEE method significantly reduces computational burden while improving control performance, making it suitable for real-time auto-optimization in unknown environments.

title: The Log is the Agent: Event-Sourced Reactive Graphs for Auditable, Forkable Agentic Systems
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure. Open-source Apache-2.0 implementation with reproducible quickstart demo, deterministic replay, fork-and-diff, and lineage tracing
summary: Most agent frameworks are built around the language model: a conversation loop comes first, then tools, then rules, and finally a logging layer bolted on for observability, with state persisted as retrievable "memory." We describe ActiveGraph, a runtime that inverts this arrangement. The append-only event log is the source of truth; the working graph is a deterministic projection of that log; and behaviors--ordinary functions, classes, LLM-backed routines, or logic attached to typed edges--react to changes in the graph and emit new events. No component instructs another; coordination happens entirely through the shared graph. This single design decision yields three properties that retrieval-and-summarization memory systems do not provide: deterministic replay of any run from its log, cheap forking that branches a run at any event without re-executing the shared prefix, and end-to-end lineage from a high-level goal down to the individual model call that produced each artifact. We present the architecture, a determinism contract that makes replay sound, and a worked diligence example whose full causal structure is reconstructable from the log alone. We discuss--without claiming to demonstrate--why this substrate is unusually well suited to self-improving agents, and how it extends the BabyAGI lineage and prior graph-memory research.

AI.tldr: ActiveGraph inverts typical agent frameworks by making an append-only event log the source of truth, with a deterministic graph projection and reactive behaviors, enabling replay, cheap forking, and end-to-end lineage.
AI.motivation: Current agent frameworks prioritize language model loops with bolted-on observability and retrieval-based memory, lacking deterministic replay, cheap branching, and full lineage tracing.
AI.method: ActiveGraph uses an append-only event log as the single source of truth, a working graph as a deterministic projection of that log, and behaviors (functions, classes, LLM routines, typed-edge logic) that react to graph changes and emit new events—coordination happens solely through the shared graph.
AI.result: Three properties: (1) deterministic replay from any log, (2) cheap forking at any event without re-executing shared prefix, (3) end-to-end lineage from high-level goals to individual model calls.
AI.conclusion: ActiveGraph provides a substrate well-suited for self-improving agents, extending BabyAGI lineage and prior graph-memory research, with a fully reconstructable causal structure from logs alone.

title: Terminal Constraint Model Predictive Control for Image-Based Visual Servoing of UAVs with Kalman Filter-Based Moment Loss Compensation
summary: Image-Based Visual Servoing (IBVS) provides an efficient vision-guided control paradigm for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) by directly regulating image-space errors. However, conventional IBVS controllers are vulnerable to two critical issues: loss of closed-loop stability near the target due to input and state constraints, and control failure caused by intermittent loss of moment-based visual features under aggressive motion. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a terminal-constraint model predictive control (TC-MPC) framework for IBVS, integrated with a Kalman filter (KF)-based state-prediction mechanism. The TC-MPC explicitly incorporates terminal-state constraints and a terminal cost into the IBVS error dynamics, ensuring recursive feasibility, improved convergence behavior, and closed-loop stability under control and state constraints. In parallel, the Kalman filter predicts the temporal evolution of image moments during short-term visual degradation, enabling the controller to preserve control continuity when moment measurements are partially unavailable. The proposed approach is validated through real-time UAV visual servoing experiments.

AI.tldr: A TC-MPC framework with Kalman filter prediction is proposed for IBVS to ensure stability under constraints and maintain control during visual feature loss, validated through real-time UAV experiments.
AI.motivation: Conventional IBVS controllers suffer from loss of closed-loop stability near the target due to input/state constraints and control failure caused by intermittent loss of moment-based visual features under aggressive motion.
AI.method: Proposes a terminal-constraint model predictive control (TC-MPC) framework with terminal-state constraints and terminal cost integrated into IBVS error dynamics, combined with a Kalman filter (KF)-based state-prediction mechanism for predicting image moments during visual degradation.
AI.result: Validated through real-time UAV visual servoing experiments, demonstrating recursive feasibility, improved convergence behavior, and closed-loop stability under constraints, as well as control continuity during partial moment measurement loss.
AI.conclusion: The TC-MPC framework with KF-based prediction effectively addresses stability and feature-loss issues in IBVS for UAVs, ensuring robust visual servoing under realistic operating conditions.

title: Active Evidence-Seeking and Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support
summary: Large language models perform well on static medical examinations, yet clinical diagnosis often requires iterative evidence gathering under uncertainty. Building on prior interactive evaluation efforts, we introduce an OSCE-inspired standardized patient simulator and a controlled, reproducible benchmark for active diagnostic inquiry. Across 468 cases and 15 models in our protocol, we observe that multi-turn evidence seeking reduces diagnostic accuracy by 12.75% and lowers supporting-evidence quality by 24.36% relative to full-context evaluation; error analyses associate these drops with premature diagnostic closure and inefficient questioning. Together, these results suggest that static full-context benchmarks may overestimate performance in interactive evidence-seeking settings, motivating complementary interactive assessment for safer clinical decision support.

AI.tldr: LLMs show reduced diagnostic accuracy (12.75% drop) and evidence quality (24.36% drop) in multi-turn interactive diagnostic settings compared to static full-context evaluations, due to premature closure and inefficient questioning, motivating interactive benchmarks for safer clinical AI.
AI.motivation: Static medical exam benchmarks may overestimate real-world LLM diagnostic performance because actual clinical diagnosis requires iterative evidence gathering under uncertainty, which is not captured by single-turn evaluations.
AI.method: Introduced an OSCE-inspired standardized patient simulator and a controlled benchmark for active diagnostic inquiry; tested 468 cases across 15 models comparing multi-turn evidence seeking vs. full-context evaluation.
AI.result: Multi-turn evidence seeking reduced diagnostic accuracy by 12.75% and supporting-evidence quality by 24.36% relative to full-context evaluation; errors were associated with premature diagnostic closure and inefficient questioning.
AI.conclusion: Static full-context benchmarks may overestimate performance in interactive clinical settings, highlighting the need for complementary interactive assessment to ensure safer clinical decision support.

title: Steins;Gate Drive: Semantic Safety Arbitration over Structured Futures for Latency-Decoupled LLM Planning
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables, submitted to IEEE transaction of intelligent vehicles
summary: Cloud-hosted LLM driver agents provide useful semantic judgments, but their inference latency exceeds stepwise vehicle-control windows. Learned world models predict futures, but they usually keep future generation and action selection inside large coupled loops. We present SteinsGateDrive, a latency-decoupled planner-runtime architecture in which the worldline metaphor from the eponymous story names one plausible consequence of an intervention: the LLM selects counterfactual driving futures before the final control instant, and a runtime reuses the selected forecast only while safety contracts remain valid. The generator builds three world-line roles: alpha nominal ego-conditioned futures, beta interaction counterfactuals around nearby vehicles, and gamma hazard-stress futures such as braking, cut-ins, or blocked corridors. The selected branch becomes a typed StrategicForecast with horizon, validity/abort conditions, fallback, and authority. On a within-subject, matched-seed normal-highway protocol with 10 seeds and 20 steps, GPT-5.4 mini reduces effective lag from +3.07 s at 1-second horizon to -0.01 s at 4-second horizon while preserving the measured no-collision safety boundary. The architecture's safety contribution comes from the atom-predicate runtime check, not from the drift score, which functions as a refresh-frequency knob.

AI.tldr: SteinsGateDrive is a latency-decoupled planner-runtime architecture for LLM-driven vehicle control that uses a worldline metaphor to pre-select counterfactual driving futures before the control instant, reducing effective latency from +3.07s to -0.01s while maintaining safety.
AI.motivation: Cloud-hosted LLM agents have high inference latency that exceeds real-time vehicle control windows, and learned world models couple future generation and action selection in large loops, making them unsuitable for stepwise control.
AI.method: The system decouples LLM planning from runtime execution using a worldline architecture: an LLM pre-selects counterfactual driving futures (alpha, beta, gamma roles) as typed StrategicForecasts with horizon, validity/abort conditions, fallback, and authority. The runtime reuses the selected forecast as long as safety contracts (atom-predicate checks) remain valid.
AI.result: On a within-subject, matched-seed normal-highway protocol with 10 seeds and 20 steps using GPT-5.4 mini, effective lag is reduced from +3.07s at 1-second horizon to -0.01s at 4-second horizon, while preserving the no-collision safety boundary.
AI.conclusion: The architecture's safety contribution comes from the atom-predicate runtime check (not the drift score, which is just a refresh-frequency knob), demonstrating that latency-decoupled worldline architectures can enable LLM agents for real-time vehicle control.

title: Enhancing Visual Token Representations for Video Large Language Models via Training-Free Spatial-Temporal Pooling and Gridding
comment: Accepted by ICLR 2026
summary: Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly advanced video understanding tasks, yet challenges remain in efficiently compressing visual tokens while preserving spatiotemporal interactions. Existing methods, such as LLaVA family, utilize simplistic pooling or interpolation techniques that overlook the intricate dynamics of visual tokens. To bridge this gap, we propose ST-GridPool, a novel training-free visual token enhancement method designed specifically for Video LLMs. Our approach integrates Pyramid Temporal Gridding (PTG), which captures multi-grained spatiotemporal interactions through hierarchical temporal gridding, and Norm-based Spatial Pooling (NSP), which preserves high-information visual regions by leveraging the correlation between token norms and semantic richness. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that ST-GridPool consistently enhances performance of Video LLMs without requiring costly retraining. Our method offers an efficient and plug-and-play solution for improving visual token representations. Our code is available in https://github.com/bingjunluo/ST-GridPool.

AI.tldr: ST-GridPool is a training-free visual token enhancement method for Video LLMs that improves performance by integrating Pyramid Temporal Gridding (multi-grained spatiotemporal interactions) and Norm-based Spatial Pooling (preserving high-information regions), without requiring costly retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA family) use simplistic pooling or interpolation techniques that overlook intricate spatiotemporal dynamics of visual tokens, leading to inefficient compression while preserving spatiotemporal interactions in video understanding tasks.
AI.method: ST-GridPool introduces two components: (1) Pyramid Temporal Gridding (PTG) for capturing multi-grained spatiotemporal interactions via hierarchical temporal gridding, and (2) Norm-based Spatial Pooling (NSP) that preserves high-information visual regions by leveraging the correlation between token norms and semantic richness. The method is training-free and plug-and-play.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that ST-GridPool consistently enhances performance of Video LLMs without requiring costly retraining.
AI.conclusion: ST-GridPool offers an efficient, training-free, plug-and-play solution for improving visual token representations in Video LLMs, bridging the gap caused by simplistic pooling/interpolation approaches in existing MLLMs.

title: Quantifying Full-Body Immersion
comment: This manuscript is under consideration for possible publication in the Nature. Copyright may be transferred to Nature if the manuscript is accepted for publication, without further notice
summary: Humanity is at the forefront of yet another digital revolution, where the lines between real and virtual worlds are dissolving, reshaping how we perceive and interact with our surroundings. In this context, we introduce a transformative paradigm for immersive virtual experiences centered around whole-body kinetic interactions. Our approach redefines immersion through three distinct levels: audio-visual immersion, capturing sensory realism; physical immersion, delivering haptic feedback; and full-body immersion (FBI), where dynamic bodily interaction integrates seamlessly with virtual environments. At the core of this innovation lies a scalable, distributable platform based on modular robotic surface units inspired by the adaptive designs of nature. These units enable the rendering of immersive environments at any scale, from intimate personal experiences to expansive multi-user settings, dynamically adapting to interactions in real-time. The modular system distributes force, shape, and motion feedback throughout entire spaces, replicating the physical characteristics of the environment and enabling new depth of engagement through FBI. By combining scalability, adaptability, and dynamic physical engagement, this framework bridges the gap between real and virtual worlds. It offers an unprecedented level of immersion where users can engage their entire bodies in symbiotic interactions with the virtual space. This work not only advances immersive technology but also redefines how humans and virtual environments coexist, setting a foundation for a new era of human-environment synthesis.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a scalable, modular robotic surface platform inspired by nature that enables three levels of immersion (audio-visual, physical, and full-body immersion) for whole-body kinetic interactions in virtual environments, bridging the gap between real and virtual worlds.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of current immersive technologies by enabling whole-body kinetic interactions and dynamic physical engagement that seamlessly integrate with virtual environments, transcending traditional audio-visual immersion.
AI.method: A scalable, distributable platform based on modular robotic surface units inspired by adaptive natural designs, which render immersive environments at any scale through dynamic force, shape, and motion feedback across entire spaces, supporting real-time interaction adaptation.
AI.result: The framework achieves three levels of immersion (audio-visual, physical, and full-body immersion) with unprecedented depth of engagement, enabling users to interact with virtual spaces using their entire bodies in real-time, symbiotic interactions.
AI.conclusion: This framework bridges the gap between real and virtual worlds, redefines human-environment coexistence, and establishes a foundation for a new era of human-environment synthesis through immersive virtual experiences.

title: A Camera-Cooperative ISAC Framework for Multimodal Non-Cooperative UAVs Sensing
summary: The detection of non-cooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) presents significant challenges for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems due to the inherent limitations of single-modal perception and the competition for shared communication and sensing resources. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Camera-Cooperative ISAC (CC-ISAC) framework that employs multimodal sensing to enable efficient UAV beam steering and tracking. The proposed framework employs cameras for coarse-grained airspace monitoring and utilizes ISAC for fine-grained, high-precision sensing, forming a complementary perception loop that enhances both sensing accuracy and resource efficiency. Within this framework, two key modules are developed: (1) a Vision-to-Echo Data Alignment (V2EDA) model that aligns visual and echo-domain features through cross-attention mechanisms, and (2) a Multimodal Fusion-Based Estimation (MMFE) model that integrates historical multimodal data with current observations for robust state estimation. Extensive evaluations conducted on the DeepSense 6G dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an average reduction of 71% in beam steering overhead and 1.69-11.15% in tracking overhead while maintaining high angular estimation accuracy. The CC-ISAC framework effectively mitigates resource contention between sensing and communication, enabling reliable UAV surveillance while freeing substantial system resources for additional communication tasks, thereby representing a practical advancement in ISAC system design.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Camera-Cooperative ISAC (CC-ISAC) framework that uses multimodal sensing (cameras + ISAC) to enhance UAV beam steering and tracking. It introduces V2EDA and MMFE models for feature alignment and state estimation, achieving 71% reduction in beam steering overhead and 1.69-11.15% in tracking overhead on the DeepSense 6G dataset.
AI.motivation: Single-modal perception and competition for shared communication/sensing resources in ISAC systems make non-cooperative UAV detection challenging.
AI.method: Proposes CC-ISAC framework with cameras for coarse monitoring and ISAC for fine sensing; includes V2EDA (cross-attention vision-to-echo alignment) and MMFE (multimodal fusion state estimation).
AI.result: 71% reduction in beam steering overhead, 1.69-11.15% reduction in tracking overhead, while maintaining high angular estimation accuracy on DeepSense 6G dataset.
AI.conclusion: CC-ISAC mitigates resource contention between sensing and communication, enabling reliable UAV surveillance while freeing resources for additional communication tasks.

title: Knowledge Graph Re-engineering Along the Ontological Continuum (extended version)
summary: Knowledge graphs have become the primary vehicle for data integration and are critical to the success of modern AI, but the diversity of KG modelling practices, from lightweight vocabularies to richly axiomatised ontologies, makes integration and reuse expensive and brittle. This challenge is particularly acute in neuro-symbolic AI, where bridging neural and symbolic components depends on the ability to reengineer KGs to fit new requirements; GenAI now offers unprecedented automation capability, but without a principled understanding of the KG space, such automation remains conceptually ungrounded. We introduce the ontological continuum as that missing conceptualisation, a theoretical construct a theoretical construct whose characterisation framework is defined by two orthogonal distinctions: semantics vs pragmatics, and properties vs affordances; together these define a vocabulary to describe, compare, navigate, and transform KGs across the full range of modelling practices. The methodological stance is empirical: rather than prescribing how KGs should be modelled, the continuum aims to define a theory of the existent, derived from observation of real-world KG engineering practices and whose structure can be made formally explicit, for example, through Formal Concept Analysis (FCA). We ground the vision through a case study on provenance knowledge, showing how a single concern manifests differently across the continuum. We articulate five open research challenges and invite the community to develop the ontological continuum as a shared research agenda.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the "ontological continuum," a conceptual framework to describe, compare, navigate, and transform knowledge graphs across varying modelling practices—from lightweight vocabularies to richly axiomatised ontologies—to enable principled automation in neuro-symbolic AI and KG reengineering.
AI.motivation: Current KG modelling practices are highly diverse (from simple vocabularies to complex ontologies), making integration, reuse, and reengineering costly and brittle; this is especially problematic for neuro-symbolic AI where bridging neural and symbolic components requires principled KG transformation. GenAI offers automation potential but lacks a grounded theoretical understanding of the KG space.
AI.method: The paper proposes the ontological continuum, a theoretical construct defined by two orthogonal axes: semantics vs pragmatics and properties vs affordances. The methodology is empirical—derived from observing real-world KG engineering practices rather than prescribing norms—and aims for formal explicitness (e.g., via Formal Concept Analysis). A case study on provenance knowledge demonstrates the framework.
AI.result: A characterisation framework with a vocabulary for describing, comparing, navigating, and transforming KGs across the full modelling spectrum; a case study showing how provenance knowledge manifests differently along the continuum; and five identified open research challenges.
AI.conclusion: The ontological continuum provides a missing conceptual grounding for principled KG reengineering and neuro-symbolic integration. The authors invite the community to adopt it as a shared research agenda to address the identified open challenges.

title: Decoupling Ego-Motion from Target Dynamics via Dual-Interval Motion Cues for UAV Detection
summary: Object detection from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is challenged by severe ego-motion, camera jitter, and large scale variations. While modern detectors perform well on static images, their direct application to UAV video often fails, particularly for small objects in dynamic scenes. Existing motion-based methods either rely on computationally expensive optical flow or use single-interval differencing, which is sensitive to jitter and limited in capturing diverse motion patterns. We propose a vision-only motion-guided detection framework that decouples target motion from camera-induced disturbances. A homography-based Global Motion Compensation (GMC) first aligns adjacent frames. We then introduce a Dual-Interval Motion Extraction strategy that captures both short-term and long-term motion cues. To integrate these cues, a lightweight Motion-Guided Attention (MGA) module enhances feature representations within a Feature Pyramid Network. Experiments on the VisDrone-VID dataset demonstrate consistent improvements over a strong YOLOv8 baseline under severe ego-motion. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the dual-interval design and the proposed motion-guided attention mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a vision-only motion-guided detection framework for UAV object detection that decouples target motion from camera-induced disturbances using homography-based Global Motion Compensation, Dual-Interval Motion Extraction, and a lightweight Motion-Guided Attention module, achieving consistent improvements over YOLOv8 on VisDrone-VID.
AI.motivation: UAV object detection suffers from severe ego-motion, camera jitter, and large scale variations. Existing motion-based methods are either computationally expensive (optical flow) or limited (single-interval differencing sensitive to jitter), motivating a more efficient and robust motion-guided approach.
AI.method: (1) Homography-based Global Motion Compensation (GMC) to align adjacent frames and decouple target motion from camera motion. (2) Dual-Interval Motion Extraction capturing both short-term and long-term motion cues. (3) Lightweight Motion-Guided Attention (MGA) module integrated into Feature Pyramid Network to enhance feature representations.
AI.result: Consistent improvements over a strong YOLOv8 baseline on the VisDrone-VID dataset under severe ego-motion; ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of dual-interval design and MGA mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The proposed vision-only framework effectively addresses UAV-specific challenges (ego-motion, jitter, scale variation) by explicitly modeling motion with a lightweight, dual-interval attention mechanism, offering a practical and efficient solution for moving object detection from UAVs.

title: MPDocBench-Parse: Benchmarking Practical Multi-page Document Parsing
